cold_first_call.definition: A cold call is the first call of a fresh process, measured as the warm-up call of the row (build_seconds of a row that is the first of its process). With the compiled caches kept, the process finds the Triton kernels and the torch extension of the HIP kernel on disk; with the caches cleared, the call compiles them, including the hipcc build of the HIP kernel.

session_note: every row is the median of 7 timed runs, with the minimum and the maximum, on one machine with the same package versions, in one session that started 2026-10-26T04:56:28Z UTC (load average 2.9) and ended at 2026-10-26T07:46:38Z UTC. Every part ran pinned to cores 0-15 on an otherwise idle machine with nothing else on the GPU: no part was stopped, resumed or run beside another job. load_at_start in a row is the one-minute load average when the row starts, so it still contains the previous row's work and is not the load of an idle machine. The versions of triton, batman and wotan were not recorded by bench.py in this session; they are those of the environment that ran it, read from that environment by importlib.metadata (triton-rocm 3.7.0, batman-package 2.5.3, wotan 1.10) and equal to the versions that the lock file of that environment pins, which did not change between 2026-10-26T00:59 local and the end of the session.
